es.summary: La warfarina es un anticoagulante oral que inhibe la síntesis hepática de factores de coagulación dependientes de vitamina K.
key_points: Se monitoriza con INR; rango terapéutico típico 2-3 o 2.5-3.5 según indicación.
Interacciones alimentarias: alimentos ricos en vitamina K pueden disminuir su efecto.
Efecto adverso principal: sangrado, que puede ser grave.
Antídoto: vitamina K1 (fitomenadiona) y plasma fresco congelado en casos de hemorragia.

mechanism: Bloquea la enzima epóxido reductasa, impidiendo la reciclación de la vitamina K.
Reduce la γ‑carboxilación de los factores II, VII, IX y X y de proteínas C y S.
indications: Prevención y tratamiento de trombosis venosa profunda y embolia pulmonar.
Prevención de eventos tromboembólicos en fibrilación auricular.
Profilaxis de trombosis en prótesis valvulares mecánicas.
contraindications: Hemorragia activa o riesgo alto de sangrado.
interactions: AINEs y aspirina potencian el riesgo de sangrado.
Alimentos ricos en vitamina K (espinaca, brócoli) disminuyen INR.
nursing_care: Obtener INR antes de cada dosis; retener warfarina si INR > rango terapéutico.
Evaluar signos de sangrado: hematuria, melena, hematomas extensos.
Verificar consumo diario de alimentos con vitamina K y mantener constancia.
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si INR < 2 o > 3.5 (según indicación).
Registrar hora y vía de administración; evitar errores de dosis.
patient_teaching: Informar que debe tomar la warfarina a la misma hora cada día.
Explicar la importancia de mantener una dieta constante en vitamina K.
Enseñar a reconocer signos de sangrado y cuándo buscar ayuda.
Indicar la necesidad de acudir a controles de INR según lo programado.
antidote_overdose: Vitamina K1 (fitomenadiona) vía oral o IV según gravedad.
Plasma fresco congelado o concentrado de complejo protrombínico para sangrado grave.

related_to: consumo de alimentos ricos en vitamina K
outcomes: Sin evidencia de sangrado activo durante la hospitalización
INR mantenido dentro del rango terapéutico especificado

interventions.action: Monitorear INR según orden médica y registrar resultados.
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar la dosis y prevenir hemorragias.

interventions.action: Evaluar diariamente signos de sangrado (p. ej., hematomas, hematuria).
Revisar la ingesta dietética de vitamina K y educar al paciente para mantener constancia.
interventions.rationale: Evita fluctuaciones del INR por cambios dietéticos.

interventions.action: Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si INR supera el rango terapéutico.
interventions.rationale: Previene sangrado grave al ajustar la terapia a tiempo.

interventions.action: Administrar vitamina K1 o plasma fresco congelado según indicación del médico en caso de sangrado significativo.

en.summary: Warfarin is an oral anticoagulant that inhibits hepatic synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors.
key_points: Monitored with INR; typical therapeutic range 2-3 or 2.5-3.5 depending on indication.
Dietary interactions: foods high in vitamin K can reduce its effect.
Primary adverse effect: bleeding, which can be severe.
Antidote: vitamin K1 (phytonadione) and fresh frozen plasma in cases of hemorrhage.

mechanism: Blocks the enzyme epoxide reductase, preventing recycling of vitamin K.
Reduces γ‑carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C and S.
indications: Prevention and treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
Prevention of thromboembolic events in atrial fibrillation.
Prophylaxis of thrombosis in mechanical valve prostheses.
contraindications: Active bleeding or high risk of bleeding.
interactions: NSAIDs and aspirin increase bleeding risk.
Foods high in vitamin K (spinach, broccoli) decrease INR.
nursing_care: Obtain INR before each dose; hold warfarin if INR > therapeutic range.
Assess for signs of bleeding: hematuria, melena, extensive bruising.
Verify daily intake of vitamin K foods and maintain consistency.
Hold dose and notify physician if INR < 2 or > 3.5 (per indication).
Record time and route of administration; avoid dosing errors.
patient_teaching: Inform that warfarin should be taken at the same time each day.
Explain importance of maintaining a consistent vitamin K diet.
Teach recognition of bleeding signs and when to seek help.
Indicate need to attend scheduled INR checks.
antidote_overdose: Vitamin K1 (phytonadione) orally or IV as severity dictates.
Fresh frozen plasma or prothrombin complex concentrate for severe bleeding.

outcomes: No evidence of active bleeding during hospitalization
INR maintained within specified therapeutic range

interventions.action: Monitor INR per physician order and record results.
interventions.rationale: Allows dose adjustment and prevents hemorrhage.

interventions.action: Daily assessment of bleeding signs (e.g., bruises, hematuria).
Review dietary vitamin K intake and educate patient to maintain consistency.
interventions.rationale: Prevents INR fluctuations due to dietary changes.

interventions.action: Hold dose and notify physician if INR exceeds therapeutic range.
interventions.rationale: Prevents severe bleeding by timely therapy adjustment.

interventions.action: Administer vitamin K1 or fresh frozen plasma as ordered by physician in case of significant bleeding.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Feminizing Hormonal Therapy

summary.0.quote: Inhibits the production of vitamin K, which is needed for synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X

key_points.1.quote: Since warfarin decreases vitamin K production, dietary intake of vitamin K opposes the anticoagulant effect and can decrease warfarin’s effect.

key_points.2.quote: The major side effect of all anticoagulant medications is bleeding complications.

sections.indications.0.quote: It is an oral drug used for the treatment of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)/PE (pulmonary embolism), stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation, and thromboembolism prophylaxis after hip arthroplasty.

sections.indications.1.quote: Prophylaxis and treatment of thromboembolic complications associated with atrial fibrillation and/or cardiac valve replacement

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Have their liver enzymes monitored for early signs of hepatotoxicity and jaundice.

sections.interactions.1.quote: Concomitant medications that further increase bleeding risk, such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (e.g., ibuprofen and naproxen) or antiplatelet agents (e.g. aspirin, discussed later in this chapter) should also be avoided with anticoagulants when possible.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: It is important for clients who take warfarin to maintain a consistent amount of vitamin K intake.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Administer warfarin at the same time each day according to institutional policies.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: The nurse should instruct the client to: Maintain a consistent amount of vitamin K in their diet.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Recognize the signs and symptoms of bleeding as described under adverse effects and notify providers immediately if any of these signs or symptoms occur.

sections.patient_teaching.3.quote: For most clients, the INR is monitored frequently during initiation and during any lifestyle or medication changes.
